I posted the test results in a Discord thread:
https://discord.com/channels/775381525260664832/867820390406422538/threads/1395349728459231316

During testing `phosphor-image-updater` crashes with the following errors:
1) `std::bad_alloc` -> sigabrt;
2) segfault.

1. @striker_1993@mail.ru I would suggest NOT to make any changes to repo versions but just take the one's which are in openbmc/openbmc and use this patch and see how it goes. Did u test with this combination?
2. Also for your testing can please add a info log before this->parent.erase(this->versionId); to see if it actually gets called. Also you can add and check the logs in https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/blob/master/bmc/item_updater.cpp#L490 erase function and see what flow is it going through?

1. Yes.
This revision: https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc/commit/0fc8d76b76
And applied your patch.

2. Changes and logs are below.

> Jul 18 19:12:02 openbmc phosphor-image-updater[21441]: terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::length_error'
> Jul 18 19:12:02 openbmc phosphor-image-updater[21441]:   what():  basic_string::_M_create

Looks like something wrong with the versionId. Can you try printing it before lambda and check the value? I don't think activation object shall go out of scope until its erased but we need to see why correct versionId/entryId is not being passed. 


Also going back to the original issue you mentioned on discord -

> ```
> Since boost::asio::io_context is not run, the downloaded activation will not be deleted, resulting in "no free space" after 3-4 iterations.
> Should it be fixed with sdbusplus::async::context spawn()?
> ```

Are you running out of flash memory?

@striker_1993@mail.ru This is already being discussed on https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/+/82088/comment/2d1ae64e_0a0c9599/. So, lets use that comment thread. Please feel free to test the requested flow in that thread and provide your feedback as this patch is specifically for old flow.

It looks like this function (`getIOContext`) is only used in this line (and was added for this code in https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/commit/258681896603d2af084e8f6bf86bc33423ed7153 ).

I don't see any other uses.
Maybe it's time to remove it completely?
Acknowledged

Hi @paligill@gmail.com, I see that the ItemUpdater::erase() function is not handling removing image folders under `/tmp/images`, is it expected? Because after many bios updates on our platform, `No space left...` appears.
Already being discussed at https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/+/82088/comment/2d1ae64e_0a0c9599/. Hence , marking this as resolved.

@anoo@us.ibm.com  Looks like ImageManager was the one to delete the images from /tmp/images dir https://grok.openbmc.org/xref/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/bmc/image_manager.cpp?r=cab87e9cdeeb3e166d6d577511f6be4dc7721aca#243. Do you know how item_updater used to call back into it or is it some other flow.

PS: This is for bios update (not BMC).

I think your observation is correct. The Version created by the ImageManager when a file was uploaded had its own erase callback that deletes the /tmp/images/<id>/ dir. But with the new code update, only the ItemUpdater Version is created, which has a erase callback that doesn't erase the /tmp/images/<id>/ dir.

Let me just confirm that the /tmp/images/<id> dir is not erased either with bmc images with OnReset option, and I think we would just need to add the logic from the ImageManager erase() into the ItemUpdater erase().

@anoo@us.ibm.com This is with the old flow with software-update-dbus-interface feature flag DISABLED. So, image_manager should still be there.

Sure in the new flow you can check and see whats the behavior.

I see.

@chaul@amperecomputing.com @Kamalesh if you could you verify a few things?. The ItemUpdater erase() function calls deleteImageManagerObject() which just calls GetObject and Delete d-bus apis. We're going to try to call them manually:

1. When you upload a bios image, check the /tmp/images/<id>/ dir is created:

```
# ls /tmp/images/
c38f873b
```

2. Check that a Delete exists under the Version interface (there'll likely be a Delete one also under the Host.Updater interface):

```
# busctl -j call xyz.openbmc_project.ObjectMapper /xyz/openbmc_project/object_mapper xyz.openbmc_project.ObjectMapper GetObject sas /xyz/openbmc_project/software/c38f873b  1 xyz.openbmc_project.Software.Version
...
			"org.open_power.Software.Host.Updater" : [
...
				"xyz.openbmc_project.Object.Delete",
...
			"xyz.openbmc_project.Software.Version" : [
...
				"xyz.openbmc_project.Object.Delete",
```

3. Check that the Path property is set to /tmp/images/<id>:

```
# busctl introspect xyz.openbmc_project.Software.BMC.Updater /xyz/openbmc_project/software/c38f873b
...
xyz.openbmc_project.Common.FilePath                interface -         -                                        -
.Path                                              property  s         "/tmp/images/c38f873b"                   emits-change writable
```

4. Try calling the Delete which is what the deleteImageManagerObject() calls:

```
# busctl call xyz.openbmc_project.Software.Version /xyz/openbmc_project/software/c38f873b xyz.openbmc_project.Object.Delete Delete
```

5. Check the /tmp/images/<id>/ dir is deleted:

```
# ls /tmp/images
```

> We're going to try to call them manually

I have tried all the steps before. I can confirm that calling Delete to the software object does not result in the /tmp/images/<id> being removed. The call is directed to ItemUpdater::erase() callback, which currently does not involve the removal.

> Let me just confirm that the /tmp/images/<id> dir is not erased either with bmc images with OnReset option

Yes, it's not removed even with OnReset option for BMC image, because when Activation is set, this [line](https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/blob/d9825681c72ef99f98371123f705fc3fdc86c913/bmc/activation.cpp#L148) also leads to ItemUdater::erase() function.

> I think we would just need to add the logic from the ImageManager erase() into the ItemUpdater erase().

I think so. In our local WA to fix this, we added an `else` condition to this [if](https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/blob/d9825681c72ef99f98371123f705fc3fdc86c913/bmc/item_updater.cpp#L533) and erase the temp folder there. Do you think this is the correct move? I'm not sure how it should be for BMC image.

> Ok, I would expect it to work in your environment since the ItemUpdater::erase() calls deleteImageManagerObject() which in turns calls the ImageManager::erase().
But at least you found that ItemUpdater::erase() is called and that we can add the deletion of the image there.

deleteImageManagerObject() in this case does not call ImageManager::erase() though, because the Version and Delete interface for this software object, which is a result of a [UpdateManager::startUpdate()](https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/blob/d9825681c72ef99f98371123f705fc3fdc86c913/bmc/update_manager.cpp#L210) call, is registered [here](https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/blob/d9825681c72ef99f98371123f705fc3fdc86c913/bmc/item_updater.cpp#L186), and the erase callback passed in is ItemUpdater::erase(), not ImagerManager's. It's a different flow than the old implementation.

> Yeah I think that will work for both old and new implementations, and for both BIOS and BMC, let's just check if the path exists so that even if the ImageManager erase is called to delete the upload path, there are no errors if it doesn't exist.

Yes. Thank you for your info. I think I should send a patch, right as it will address the part of issue `https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/issues/16`, which will partly be fixed by this patch if the segmentation fault issue of it is addressed.

> > Ok, I would expect it to work in your environment since the ItemUpdater::erase() calls deleteImageManagerObject() which in turns calls the ImageManager::erase().
> But at least you found that ItemUpdater::erase() is called and that we can add the deletion of the image there.
> 
> deleteImageManagerObject() in this case does not call ImageManager::erase() though, because the Version and Delete interface for this software object, which is a result of a [UpdateManager::startUpdate()](https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/blob/d9825681c72ef99f98371123f705fc3fdc86c913/bmc/update_manager.cpp#L210) call, is registered [here](https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/blob/d9825681c72ef99f98371123f705fc3fdc86c913/bmc/item_updater.cpp#L186), and the erase callback passed in is ItemUpdater::erase(), not ImagerManager's. It's a different flow than the old implementation.

@chaul@amperecomputing.com UpdaterManager won't be used in the old flow (software-update-dbus-interface as disabled). On this patch we are trying to understand and fix the image deletion issue in the old flow. So, lets keep the UpdateManager flow separate (which we will address on a separate patch). As @anoo@us.ibm.com asked can you please confirm in old flow  if following sequence is getting triggered or not -

ItemUpdater::erase() -> Activation::deleteImageManagerObject() - calls -> ImageManager delete.

https://grok.openbmc.org/xref/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/bmc/item_updater.cpp?r=01ba956256e45b953c78591319a5f25ff4ba618d#522


> 
> > Yeah I think that will work for both old and new implementations, and for both BIOS and BMC, let's just check if the path exists so that even if the ImageManager erase is called to delete the upload path, there are no errors if it doesn't exist.
> 
> Yes. Thank you for your info. I think I should send a patch, right as it will address the part of issue `https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/issues/16`, which will partly be fixed by this patch if the segmentation fault issue of it is addressed.

@aadriance@nvidia.com My suggestion is to keep the old flow as such to keep the old design consistent and we can try to figure out whats broken there as @chaul@amperecomputing.com was referring to new flow in previous chat, so that seems to be the mis-understanding. 
For new flow (software-update-dbus-interface enabled) case we can raise a separate patch to handle the image deleteion directly in erase function by adding a check for "if (!useUpdateDBusInterface)".
Please let me know your thoughts?
Kamalesh Can you please help test and verify the flow mentioned in my last comment. Thanks

Marking this as resolved since i haven't heard back and the last comment from Kamalesh as per https://discord.com/channels/775381525260664832/1395349728459231316/1399291253769637930 which says that it works.
This works on our platform.

@chaul@amperecomputing.com Can you please confirm if you are referring to the old flow(software-update-dbus-interface DISABLED) or new flow(software-update-dbus-interface ENABLED) here when you say its working for you?

I tested this via Redfish with phosphor-software-manager's `software-update-dbus-interface` ENABLED, and the bmcweb's option `redfish-updateservice-use-dbus` enabled also. So the flow is the image's memfd is transferred via D-Bus and then StartUpdate is called.
So, that is new flow. I will mark this comment as resolved because this patch is for old flow and would let Kamalesh verify and share his findings on the other comment thread.
